Switchyard

One provider list for all your coding agents.
Set up a custom model provider once, then copy it into OpenCode, Z-Code, Pi and T3 Code in one click.

```bash npx @spacatty/switchyard ``` Switchyard finds each agent's config, starts a local web UI on `127.0.0.1` and opens your browser. Works on macOS, Linux and Windows with Node.js 18+, with no dependencies. ## Why Every coding agent ("harness") keeps custom providers in its own format: OpenCode's `provider` block, Z-Code's provider and model rules, Pi's `models.json`, T3 Code's provider instances. Adding the same OpenRouter, DeepInfra or self-hosted endpoint to each one means typing the same model IDs, context limits and prices again, in a different shape every time. Switchyard reads them all, shows them as one list, and writes each format for you. ## Shared providers Every custom provider from every agent, merged by endpoint URL. For each agent you see: - **✓ id**: the agent has the provider and all its models - **+N**: it has the provider but is missing N models; click to add them - **Copy**: it doesn't have it yet; click to add it with all its models - **Not supported**: the agent can't use this kind of endpoint (see T3 Code below) Open a row to pick individual models and copy only those.

Copying is safe to repeat: it reuses the provider the agent already has for that URL, adds only missing models, and never overwrites an existing API key or headers. **Library.** Providers you add with **Add by hand** or **Add from endpoint** on this page are kept in Switchyard's own file, so they stay listed even when no agent has them yet. Any provider can be saved there with **Save to library**. ## Add a provider from its endpoint Paste a base URL (OpenRouter, DeepInfra, Together, Groq, vLLM, LiteLLM, LM Studio, Ollama…) and an optional key. Switchyard calls `/models`, then fills in each model's context and output limits, pricing, reasoning, tool and vision support from the endpoint and [models.dev](https://models.dev). Filter, tick the ones you want, done. Embedding, image and TTS models are flagged so you don't add them by accident.

## An editor for each agent Switch between agents in the sidebar. | OpenCode | Z-Code | Pi | |---|---|---| | | | | | Providers and models, default and small model, every other setting (built from the live `opencode.ai/config.json` schema), `AGENTS.md`, agents and commands, raw JSON. | Custom providers and their models, including reasoning levels and image, PDF and video input. Chat completions, Responses and Anthropic APIs. | Providers, models, limits, reasoning, image input and prices, plus raw JSON for `compat`, `thinkingLevelMap` and the rest. | **T3 Code** has a smaller editor: base URL, key, on/off and a list of model IDs, plus raw JSON for the instance. Every OpenCode, Z-Code and Pi model row has a **test** button that sends a tiny request to check the model answers. ## API keys between agents Each agent stores keys differently, so copying converts them: | Stored as | OpenCode | Pi | Z-Code and T3 Code | |---|---|---|---| | Env variable | `{env:VAR}` | `$VAR` | the variable's value, as plain text (they can't read variables) | | File | `{file:path}` | the file's contents, as plain text | the file's contents, as plain text | | Command (Pi `!cmd`) | not copied | `!cmd` | not copied | Switchyard tells you whenever a copy stored a key as plain text or couldn't copy it. ## Files it edits | Agent | Default path | |---|---| | OpenCode | `$OPENCODE_CONFIG`, `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json(c)` (on Windows too), or the project's `opencode.json(c)` / `.opencode/opencode.json(c)`. Switch between them in the sidebar. | | Z-Code | `~/.zcode/v2/provider_config.json` (or `$ZCODE_DATA_BASE_DIR/.zcode/v2/…`) | | Pi | `~/.pi/agent/models.json` (or `$PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR/models.json`) | | T3 Code | `~/.t3/userdata/settings.json` (or `$T3CODE_HOME/userdata/settings.json`) | | Library | `~/.config/switchyard/providers.json` (respects `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME`) | Every write makes a `.bak` first and replaces the file atomically, and each config is checked against what its agent would reject before it's written. Z-Code, Pi, T3 Code and library files are written owner-only (`0600`). **Z-Code:** quit it (including the tray icon) before saving or copying to it. Z-Code keeps its providers in memory and rewrites its file when it exits, which would undo your changes. Switchyard warns you while it's running. **Pi:** re-reads `models.json` every time you open `/model`, so no restart is needed. Pi hides a provider's models if it has no key, so keyless endpoints get the placeholder key `none`. **T3 Code:** runs other agents rather than calling models itself, so a custom endpoint becomes an extra Claude Code provider in T3, alongside your normal one. That means only endpoints speaking the Anthropic API can be copied there. For OpenAI-style endpoints, copy them to OpenCode or Pi and turn that provider on in T3 Code. T3 picks up changes without a restart. Endpoints without a key get the placeholder token `none`, so Claude Code doesn't send your own login to them. Only model IDs and names carry over, and a key T3 has moved to its secret store is never read or replaced. ## Options ``` npx @spacatty/switchyard [options] -c, --config OpenCode config (default: auto-detect) --zcode-config Z-Code provider_config.json --pi-config Pi models.json --t3-config T3 Code settings.json --library Switchyard's provider library -p, --port Port (default 4747, falls back to a free one) --no-open Don't open the browser ``` To install it as a `switchyard` command: ```bash npm i -g @spacatty/switchyard ``` Switchyard used to be `@spacatty/occ-manager`; the `occ-manager` command still works. ## Security - The server listens on `127.0.0.1` only, checks the `Host` header, and requires a random per-session token, so other sites open in your browser can't talk to it. - API keys are only ever sent to the endpoint you entered, and never logged. ## Development ```bash git clone https://github.com/spacatty/switchyard cd switchyard # Point all five paths at scratch files, never at your real configs: node bin/cli.js --config /tmp/sy/opencode.json --zcode-config /tmp/sy/zc.json --pi-config /tmp/sy/pi.json --t3-config /tmp/sy/t3.json --library /tmp/sy/lib.json ``` | Command | What it does | |---|---| | `npm start` | Run the CLI | | `npm test` | End-to-end smoke test (needs network: hits OpenRouter `/models` and opencode.ai) | | `npm run check-schema` | Compare the live OpenCode schema with the bundled snapshot | | `npm run update-schema` | Refresh the bundled snapshot in `schema/` | The UI in `public/` is plain HTML, CSS and JS with no build step. See [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) for the code layout, how to add another agent, and the rules contributors (human or AI) follow. ## License [MIT](LICENSE)
